paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. Chronicles stops to write down a long line of names, and God lets every one of them be remembered. Perez, Hezron, Hur, Shimei and the rest all get a place in the record (1 Chronicles 4:1, 4:26). When it feels like nobody sees you, this chapter says the God of Israel keeps good records.

Then right in the middle, the list slows down for one man. Jabez was "more honorable than his brothers," and his mother had named him Jabez, saying, "Because I bore him in pain" (1 Chronicles 4:9). Then he called out to the God of Israel: "If only You would bless me and enlarge my territory! May Your hand be with me and keep me from harm, so that I will be free from pain." His name spoke of pain, his prayer asked to be free from pain, and "God granted the request of Jabez" (1 Chronicles 4:10).

The Simeonites close out the chapter. Their whole clan did not become "as numerous as the sons of Judah" (1 Chronicles 4:27), but the leaders' families "increased greatly" (1 Chronicles 4:38), and they found land that was "spacious, peaceful, and quiet" (1 Chronicles 4:40). So a smaller clan still gets its names written down and a place to live, and the record says they "have lived there to this day" (1 Chronicles 4:43). I spent years in a dark drawer feeling forgotten, baker, so a record that holds every name is good news to me.
